0.value:
cv_camera brings a live camera into the patch, as a stream of pictures.

THE NAMES:
cv_camera and cv_capture are the same node.

IT IS A TAP YOU TURN ON:
Tick 'on/off' and frames start arriving, one per frame of the patch as far as the camera keeps up, as RGB arrays. Untick it and the frames stop.

Unticking also lets go of the camera: its light goes off and other applications can use it. Ticking again reopens it, which takes a moment. Choosing a different 'source' while on switches cameras at once; while off it just sets which camera the next tick opens.

'source' lists the cameras it found. On a laptop that is usually just the built in one; plug in another and press 'refresh' to look again.

REFRESHING PROBES EVERY CAMERA, ONE BY ONE:
'refresh' finds cameras by trying to OPEN each index in turn, from 0 to 9. There is no polite way to ask; that is how it has to be done.

Two consequences. It takes a moment, and it briefly opens every camera on the machine - so an indicator light may flicker on a camera you are not using, and another application holding one may see it disturbed. The node refreshes once when it is created, and after that only when you press the button.

WHAT COMES OUT IS RGB, ALREADY CONVERTED:
OpenCV works in BGR - blue, green, red - a long-standing quirk of the library and a reliable source of pictures with skin tones gone blue. cv_camera converts to RGB before sending, so everything downstream gets the ordinary order.

If you ever hand an array to an OpenCV function yourself, it will expect BGR and you will have to convert back.

THE ARRAY IS HEIGHT, WIDTH, CHANNELS:
Frames arrive as (height, width, 3) bytes - rows first. Most of the image nodes here expect channels FIRST, and guess when they are handed the other order; the guess is right for anything camera-sized. See the k. and tv. pages for when it is not.

WHAT TO PUT AFTER IT:
A camera at thirty frames a second is a lot of data, and most of what you might do with it does not need every frame or the full resolution. Anything expensive downstream - a vision model, a large filter - is better fed from a subsample, and the vision_describe nodes will drop frames by themselves rather than fall behind.

SYNTAX:
cv_camera
cv_capture

EXAMPLE:
cv_camera

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

on/off:
Whether frames are sent. On opens the camera, off releases it.

source:
Which camera, by index. Choosing one while on switches to it.

refresh:
Look for cameras again. Opens each one to find out.

OUTPUTS:

The single outlet carries the picture, as an RGB array of height by width by 3.

RELATED:
cv_image for a still picture from a file; it used to share this page. movie_player for recorded video.
vision_describe to get words out of what the camera sees. k. and tv. nodes for filtering and adjusting the image. mgl_texture and the gl nodes to put it on screen.
